newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to start Tabriz petrochemical plant operation.
newsitem.headline: Iran to start Tabriz petrochemical plant operation.

text.p: Iran's new petrochemical plant at Tabriz should be fully operational by February 10, the manager of the complex was on Tuesday reported as saying.

Tabriz Petrochemical Complex (TPC) would yield approximately an anuual 500,000 tonnes of petrochemical byproducts, of which 300,000 tonnes would be plastics and rubber, Abbas Sedqi, TPC managing director, told Mash'al which is the weekly bulletin of Iran's state oil ministry.

"The polystyrene plant with a nominal capacity of 95,000 tonnes is exceptional in the Middle East," Sedqi said. Iran is the Middle East's second largest petrochemical producer after Saudi Arabia and aims to triple its annual output to 30 million tonnes in 25 years.

Under Iran's current five-year plan (1995-2000) the National Petrochemical Company (NPC) is to increase capacity to 15 million tonnes from the present 10 million tonnes with the construction of five new petrochemical plants.
The Tabriz plant had cost $1.106 billion plus 2,100 billion rials and would save Iran $1 million in hard currency spending on petrochemical imports, Sedqi said.
